title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-sophie-lee
content:
Personal scratchpad for debugging a model loading failure encountered during a Dedicated deployment test. Mostly breadcrumbs: commands I ran, error snippets, quick hypotheses, and next steps. Not polished.

Context:
- Deploying 13B model variant (open-architecture checkpoint) to dedicated pool on staging. Model files hosted in internal S3 bucket s3://redwood-models/staging/13b/v2/.
- Loading fails during startup on one of the nodes (node-7). Other nodes load fine initially, but intermittent failures occur for node-7 and sometimes node-3.
- Suspect: corrupted shard(s) or partial multipart upload / inconsistent manifest; also possible mismatch of checkpoint format (torch vs safetensors) or shard ordering.

Observed symptoms:
- Runtime fails during torch.load() with pickle/truncation errors or during into-device allocation with tensor size mismatches.
- Occurs early in model init (loading first few shards).

Notes from quick checks:
- aws s3 ls and aws s3api head-object show expected Content-Length for most shards, but one shard (ckpt_shard_4.bin) is ~2.1GB while expected ~2.4GB per manifest.
- md5/sha256 mismatches reported locally after download attempt for ckpt_shard_4.
- When I re-copied the same file from backup, problem moved to ckpt_shard_6 on node-3. Possible network flakiness during s3 download or intermittent disk write corruption?

Commands tried (copied from shell history):
- aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models/staging/13b/v2/ --summarize --human-readable
- aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-models --key staging/13b/v2/ckpt_shard_4.bin
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/staging/13b/v2/ckpt_shard_4.bin /tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin
- md5sum /tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin
- sha256sum /tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin
- ls -lh /tmp/ckpt_shard_*.bin
- file /tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin
- python -c 'import torch; torch.load("/tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin")'
- python -c 'from safetensors import safe_open; safe_open("/tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin", framework="pt")'
- s3cmd --acl-private get s3://redwood-models/staging/13b/v2/ckpt_shard_4.bin /tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/staging/13b/v2/ /tmp/model-checkpoint/ --recursive --exclude '*' --include 'ckpt_shard_*.bin' --no-progress
- aws s3 sync s3://redwood-models/staging/13b/v2/ /tmp/model-checkpoint/ --exact-timestamps
- curl -I https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/staging/13b/v2/ckpt_shard_4.bin
- python tools/check_manifest_checksum.py --manifest manifest.json --dir /tmp/model-checkpoint/
- dd if=/tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin of=/tmp/ckpt_shard_4.part count=1 bs=1M
commands_tried: python -c 'from safetensors import safe_open; safe_open("/tmp/ckpt_shard_4.bin", framework="pt")'
error_snippets: RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading object
torch._utils._rebuild_tensor_v2: IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 0
ValueError: tensor size mismatch, expected numel 12345678 but got 0
quick_observations: Shard sizes: most shards ~2.4GB; shard_4 consistently 2.1GB on node-7 after download
Checksum mismatch on shard_4 compared to manifest; other shards match
When re-copying the same S3 object to node-3, different shard failed (shard_6) — suggests transient network/disk corruption during copy rather than a single bad source object
S3 head-object Content-Length sometimes reports expected size, but downloaded bytes differ — possible multipart incomplete or race during upload
No recent change to model conversion tool noted in PRs, but runtime PR 1287 touched loader fallback code (linked) — keep in mind
hypotheses: Partial/failed multipart S3 uploads left some shards truncated on the source bucket (manifest inconsistent)
Transient networking / disk I/O errors during aws s3 cp on some nodes produce corrupted local files
Checkpoint format mismatch: some files are safetensors but loader tries torch.load() (or vice versa) leading to parser errors
Sharding order mismatch due to renamed shard filenames causing the runtime to reassemble tensors incorrectly
Bug in our streaming loader that doesn't check full read length / drops last bytes on slow connections
investigation_steps_completed: Compared Content-Length from s3api head-object to local file sizes
Verified md5/sha256 for all shards on a known-good backup (backup bucket) — backup matches manifest
Re-downloaded individual shards using s3cmd and aws cli to rule out client bug — still intermittent failures
Tried safetensors.safe_open and torch.load locally to see different error modes
Checked kernel/dmesg on node-7 for I/O errors (none obvious besides single soft ECC warning)
next_steps: 1) Quarantine current staging S3 prefix and restore from backup bucket which verified checksums. Update manifest to point to restored files (if restore fast).
2) Run aws s3 cp with --expected-size/--part-size adjustments and s3api to confirm object ETags; consider re-upload using singlepart for suspect shards
3) Add a pre-flight checksum step to our deploy agent: after download, verify sha256 of each shard against manifest before attempting to load. Fail fast and retry download if mismatch.
4) Instrument runtime loader to log bytes read per shard and include Content-Length from the HTTP response in logs for debugging. Add a metric for 'shard_truncated' events.
5) Re-run deployment on node-7 with strace on aws cli process to see if transfers are interrupted, and capture network stats (ifstat, tcpdump) during download.
6) If format confusion suspected, add detection: try safetensors header sniff before calling torch.load(), and fail with clear message if mismatch.
7) Coordinate with storage infra to check S3 multipart upload logs for the timeframe of model push (ticket INF-3421 linked)
8) Add a temporary retry wrapper in the deploy script that re-downloads a shard up to 3x if checksum fails, with exponential backoff
notes_to_self: - Talk to @Jordan about making manifest verifier part of CI for model pushes
- Follow up with storage infra about multipart reassembly logs
- If we confirm node disk flakiness, mark node-7 for deeper hardware check
- Keep PR 1287 on watch; add unit tests for the loader fallback code paths
